descriptionChirho: Sustained effort and devoted eagerness in pursuing a goal, especially in moral and spiritual life (σπουδή as earnest care). Used in exhortations to show diligence in faith, love, and good works (Romans 12:8, 2 Corinthians 7:11-12, 2 Peter 1:5, Hebrews 6:11). Multilingual evidence: Arabic اجْتِهَاد (ijtihād, 'striving/diligence'), Korean 열심 (yeolsim, 'zeal/enthusiasm'), Swahili bidii ('diligence/effort'), Hindi लगन (lagan, 'devotion')/तत्परता (tatparatā, 'readiness'), Spanish diligencia. This is a dispositional quality, not a temporal urgency.

Quickness of action driven by pressing circumstances, physical hurry or rush (σπουδή as speed/haste). Used in Luke 1:39 (Mary's hurried journey to Elizabeth) and Mark 6:25 (Herodias's daughter rushing back with her request). Multilingual evidence clearly distinguishes this from the 'diligence' sense: Arabic عَجَلَة (ʿajala, 'hurry')/سُرْعَة (surʿa, 'speed'), Korean 서둘러 (seodulleo, 'hurriedly'), Swahili haraka ('haste/speed'), Hindi जल्दी (jaldī, 'quickly'), Spanish prisa ('rush/hurry'). The distinction is temporal urgency rather than sustained devotion.
